chunks: Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah narrated from his father, from Abdillah ibn al-Mughirah, from Burayd al-Ijli, who said:

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), 'I have a debt upon me, and I think it is for orphans, and I fear that if I sell my estate, I will remain with nothing.' He said, 'Do not sell your estate, but give from it [to pay the debt] and retain some for yourself.'

key_terms.أَبُو عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), referring to Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq

ai.seo_question: How should one repay a debt if selling all assets would leave them with nothing?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) provides a practical legal ruling for debtors facing destitution, prioritizing the preservation of the debtor's livelihood over the creditor's full immediate claim. This reflects the Shia juristic principle of *al-‘awn ‘ala al-ma’ruf* (facilitating good) and the concept of *al-‘usr* (hardship), ensuring that paying the debt does not lead to the debtor's ruin. The advice to 'give some and keep some' establishes a precedent for proportional repayment based on remaining capacity, balancing the rights of the orphans with the debtor's basic needs.
